title: How a generation request flows

nodes.label: Side panel + popup
nodes.note: React UI with tabs for generating tweets, analyzing a profile, personas, history and settings. Calls the backend through src/lib/api.ts.

nodes.label: Content scripts on X
nodes.note: A MutationObserver injects AI Reply, quote and viral actions into x.com compose flows. replyComposer, quote and viral call generateVariants directly.

nodes.label: Service worker
nodes.note: Manifest V3 background script: opens the side panel, opens the profile tab for tweet scraping, relays EXTRACT_* progress messages and handles media downloads.

nodes.label: chrome.storage.local
nodes.note: Holds settings, the Supabase session and a local generation history. The extension never keeps a provider key here.

nodes.label: FastAPI app
nodes.note: main.py: CORS for x.com and a chrome-extension origin regex, a lifespan hook that connects Redis, a /health route and the /v1 routers.

nodes.label: JWT verification
nodes.note: core/auth.py: fetches Supabase's JWKS (cached with a TTL), accepts RS256 or ES256 tokens only, and exposes get_current_user. A dev bypass flag exists.

nodes.label: Rate limiter
nodes.note: core/rate_limit.py: per-minute counters for each user and each IP using INCR and EXPIRE, falling back to in-memory counters if Redis errors.

nodes.label: Generation service
nodes.note: Builds the system and user prompts from mode, tone, hook style, goal, emotion and profile. Expects exactly 3 JSON variants, retries once with a repair prompt.

nodes.label: Profile analysis
nodes.note: Cleans and dedupes scraped tweets, then runs three LLM passes (structure, vocabulary, persona), each retried once, and merges them into a voice profile.

nodes.label: Key vault
nodes.note: Encrypts each provider key with Fernet (key derived from TWEETMIND_ENCRYPTION_KEY) before storing it and returns only the last four characters.

nodes.label: History + personas
nodes.note: Writes each generation to history and serves the history and persona CRUD routes. A failed history write is logged and does not fail the request.

nodes.label: Usage tracker
nodes.note: Counts generations and approximate tokens per user per day against a daily limit (default 200).

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres
nodes.note: Tables user_provider_keys, voice_profiles and generation_history, plus personas. Accessed over PostgREST with a service-role key from infra/supabase_store.py.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.note: Rate-limit counters (rl:user, rl:ip) and daily usage hashes (usage:<user>:<date>, kept 7 days).

nodes.label: User's LLM provider
nodes.note: provider_adapter.py calls OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq or OpenRouter over httpx with the user's own key.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth
nodes.note: Email and Google sign-in through supabase-js. Google goes via chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow. Issues the JWT the backend verifies.

nodes.label: X (x.com)
nodes.note: The page the content scripts read from and write into. Profile tweets are scraped from here in a tab opened by the service worker.

flow: A content script or the side panel sends the idea and its parameters to POST /v1/generate/tweet with the Supabase access token.
The backend verifies the JWT against Supabase's cached JWKS, then checks the per-user and per-IP rate limits in Redis.
The route checks that a provider key exists and that the daily generation limit is not used up. The key vault decrypts the key.
The generation service builds the prompt from the idea, voice profile and parameters and calls the chosen provider.
It expects exactly three variants as JSON. If not, it makes one repair call at a lower temperature, then filters variants against the blocklist.
Usage is recorded in Redis, the result is written to history in Supabase, and the three variants go back to the extension.
Secondary path: analyzing a profile makes the service worker open the profile in a tab, scrape tweets and relay progress. The backend then runs its three analysis passes and saves the voice profile.
